cards.question: What is suffering?
cards.answer: Suffering is the experience of pain, loss, and sorrow that entered the world through sin.

cards.question: Why does suffering exist?
cards.answer: Suffering exists because humanity fell from fellowship with God, and the whole creation was subjected to futility.

cards.question: Is all suffering the same?
cards.answer: No. Some suffering comes from our own sin, some from the sins of others, and some from living in a broken world.

cards.question: Does God cause suffering?
cards.answer: God is not the author of evil, but He sovereignly ordains all things, including suffering, for His wise and holy purposes.

cards.question: Has anyone ever suffered apart from sin?
cards.answer: Only the Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered though He was sinless, to redeem sinners and bring them to God.

cards.question: Why does God allow His people to suffer?
cards.answer: He allows suffering to display His glory, test and deepen our faith, and conform us to the image of His Son.

cards.question: Does suffering mean God has forsaken us?
cards.answer: No. For those in Christ, suffering is never a sign of abandonment but of Fatherly love and refinement.

cards.question: Can a believer question or lament in suffering?
cards.answer: Yes. Honest lament is the language of faith, bringing grief before God in trust, not rebellion.

cards.question: What makes suffering meaningful?
cards.answer: Suffering finds meaning only in relationship to the sovereign and suffering Savior, Jesus Christ.

cards.question: What hope sustains the believer in suffering?
cards.answer: The hope that Christ has overcome the world, and that present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory to come.

cards.question: Who reigns over suffering?
cards.answer: The Lord God Almighty reigns over every moment of suffering; nothing happens apart from His sovereign will.

cards.question: Is God good even when we suffer?
cards.answer: Yes. God is always good and does good, even when His purposes are hidden from our sight.

cards.question: Does God control all suffering?
cards.answer: Yes. God ordains the limits, duration, and purpose of every trial, and He turns even evil for the good of His people.

cards.question: Can anything happen to the believer by chance?
cards.answer: Nothing comes by chance; all things are directed by the hand of our loving Father.

cards.question: Does God owe us explanations for our suffering?
cards.answer: No. God is not obligated to explain His ways, but He invites us to trust His character when we cannot trace His hand.

cards.question: Is God distant in our suffering?
cards.answer: Never. He is near to the brokenhearted and saves the crushed in spirit.

cards.question: How does God relate to human pain?
cards.answer: He enters into our pain through the incarnation of His Son, who knows our weakness and carries our sorrows.

cards.question: Does God delight in our suffering?
cards.answer: No. God does not delight in the suffering itself but in the holy fruit it produces—trust, humility, endurance and hope.

cards.question: How should we view the providence of God in suffering?
cards.answer: With reverence and rest, knowing that His providence is neither blind fate nor cold determinism, but the wise care of a loving Father.

cards.question: What truth anchors the believer’s heart in affliction?
cards.answer: That God reigns, God is good, God is near, and God will not waste one tear of His redeemed children.

cards.question: How does God draw near to the suffering?
cards.answer: God draws near through His Son, Jesus Christ, who entered our world of sorrow to redeem and comfort His people.

cards.question: Did Jesus experience suffering?
cards.answer: Yes. Jesus suffered in body and soul, bearing grief, rejection, and pain, and was even deeply troubled by it, that He might become our merciful High Priest.

cards.question: Why did the Son of God suffer?
cards.answer: He suffered to take the punishment of our sin, to destroy death, and to bring us to God.

cards.question: Does Jesus understand my pain?
cards.answer: Yes. He is able to sympathize with every weakness, for He has been tested in every way yet without sin.

cards.question: How does Christ’s suffering help us?
cards.answer: His suffering shows the depth of His love, secures our redemption, and teaches us to trust our Father in trials.

cards.question: Where is Christ when I suffer?
cards.answer: Christ is present by His Spirit, interceding for you and sustaining you with grace that cannot fail.

cards.question: What does the Holy Spirit do for the suffering believer?
cards.answer: He comforts the heart, strengthens faith, and assures us we are God’s children even in affliction.

cards.question: What comfort does the gospel bring to the sufferer?
cards.answer: That the One who bore our griefs now reigns over them, and nothing can separate us from His love.

cards.question: What example did Christ leave for us in suffering?
cards.answer: He entrusted Himself to the One who judges justly, overcame evil with steadfast obedience, and set the pattern for us to follow in obedience to God, by not returning evil for evil, but doing good.

cards.question: What promise assures us of God’s nearness?
cards.answer: “I will never leave you nor forsake you,” says the Lord, whose presence is our peace.

cards.question: What is God’s purpose in the suffering of His people?
cards.answer: God uses suffering to make His people more like Christ, deepening faith, producing holiness, endurance and hope.

cards.question: How does suffering reveal our hearts?
cards.answer: Suffering exposes what we love, trust, and treasure, revealing the desires and conflicts within that show where our hope truly lies.

cards.question: What does suffering teach us about sin?
cards.answer: It teaches us that sin is destructive and that only God’s grace can heal what is broken.

cards.question: How does suffering produce endurance?
cards.answer: By teaching us to rely on God’s strength rather than our own and to persevere in faith when comfort is absent.

cards.question: How does suffering shape our character?
cards.answer: It refines our faith like gold, growing humility, patience, and compassion for others.

cards.question: How does suffering strengthen hope?
cards.answer: Through trials, we learn that this world cannot satisfy and that eternal glory far outweighs present pain.

cards.question: Does suffering make us more dependent on God?
cards.answer: Yes. In weakness we discover God’s power, and in affliction we learn that His grace is sufficient.

cards.question: What happens when we resist God in suffering?
cards.answer: We forfeit peace and growth, revealing pride that trusts self over God, allowing bitterness to take root instead of trust and repentance.

cards.question: What happens when we submit to God in suffering?
cards.answer: We find rest for our souls, joy in trials, and a deeper communion with Christ who suffered for us.

cards.question: How should believers interpret suffering in light of the cross?
cards.answer: The cross proves that God brings life through death, victory through weakness, and glory through pain.

cards.question: What comfort does God give to His suffering people?
cards.answer: God comforts us by His presence, His promises, and His people, assuring us that He is with us in every trial.

cards.question: What role does Scripture play in our suffering?
cards.answer: The Word of God revives the weary soul, teaches us in our affliction, interprets our pain rightly, and anchors our hope in His truth.

cards.question: How does prayer sustain us in affliction?
cards.answer: Prayer draws our hearts to God, turns despair into dependence, and teaches us to rest in His will.

cards.question: What if we cannot find words to pray?
cards.answer: The Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.

cards.question: How does the church comfort the suffering?
cards.answer: The church bears one another’s burdens, weeps with those who weep, and reminds the hurting of God’s steadfast love.

cards.question: Why must suffering not be faced alone?
cards.answer: Because Christ designed His people for fellowship, where comfort multiplies and faith is strengthened together.

cards.question: What part does worship play in enduring suffering?
cards.answer: Worship lifts our eyes from pain to the beauty of God, teaching us to rejoice even in the midst of sorrow.

cards.question: How does remembering God’s faithfulness bring comfort?
cards.answer: Remembering His past mercies strengthens present trust, fuels future hope, and, in the testimony of the saints, displays His glory to help others endure.

cards.question: How should we speak to one another in times of suffering?
cards.answer: With gentleness and grace-filled truth, speaking words seasoned with wisdom that offer the same comfort we have received from God.

cards.question: What promise enables believers to persevere through suffering?
cards.answer: That the God who began a good work in us will carry it on to completion in Christ Jesus.

cards.question: Will suffering last forever?
cards.answer: No. For those in Christ, every sorrow will end when death is destroyed and all things are made new.

cards.question: What happens to the believer after death?
cards.answer: The believer’s soul departs to be with Christ, which is far better, while the body rests until the resurrection.

cards.question: What hope awaits the church at Christ’s return?
cards.answer: The resurrection of the body, the renewal of creation, and the everlasting joy of dwelling with God.

cards.question: How does this future hope shape our present suffering?
cards.answer: It teaches us that present afflictions are light and momentary, preparing us for an eternal weight of glory.

cards.question: What will happen to pain and tears in the new creation?
cards.answer: God Himself will wipe away every tear, and pain, sorrow, and death shall be no more.

cards.question: What will we see in the age to come?
cards.answer: We will see the face of Christ, our Redeemer, and be perfectly satisfied in His glory forever.

cards.question: How does the hope of glory purify us now?
cards.answer: Those who hope in Christ’s appearing purify themselves, living in holiness as He is holy.

cards.question: What song will the redeemed sing in eternity?
cards.answer: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain, for He has redeemed us by His blood and made us a kingdom of priests to our God.”

cards.question: What will the end of all suffering reveal?
cards.answer: The perfect wisdom, goodness, and faithfulness of God, who works all things for His glory and our joy in Him.

cards.question: How should believers live while they wait for glory?
cards.answer: With endurance, joy, and steadfast faith, fixing their eyes on Jesus, the founder and perfecter of their faith.
